visible_observation: The layout features a clean, editorial grid with a serif headline and sans-serif body text. The three headline indicators use distinct accent colors (red, teal, blue) that correspond to the charts below. The 'Monthly rainfall & flood risk' chart uses a bar graph with a background highlight for the 'HIGH FLOOD RISK WINDOW'.
critique: The 'HIGH FLOOD RISK WINDOW' label in the rainfall chart is visually compromised. It is rendered in a light red/pink color that has very low contrast against the light pink background of the flood window itself. Furthermore, the text is positioned directly behind the data labels (290, 277) and the top of the bars, creating a cluttered and hard-to-read collision that breaks the visual hierarchy.
revision: Move the 'HIGH FLOOD RISK WINDOW' label to the top-left corner of the pink background area, outside the bar cluster. Change the text color to a dark, high-contrast red (e.g., #991111) to ensure legibility against the light background.
protected_strength: The consistent use of the three accent colors (red for heat, teal for rain, blue for sea) across the indicator cards and the charts below them is a strong system element that must be preserved.
